newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- DEC 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- DEC 11.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:
KATHIMERINI

--The country's exports and production is now being hard hit by the continuing blockade of national roads by the farmers. Figures show clearly that many industries are either working below capacity or have suspended operations due to the lack of raw materials. According to exporters, the 13-day-old blockade has effectively cancelled 80 percent of exports, leading to the non-export of six billion drachmas of Greek goods daily.

--Tourist exchange inflows were down 15 percent in the first half 1996, reflecting the fall in visitors this year. According to the Bank of Greece, tourist inflows in June were 398 million dollars, against 772.8 million in the corresponding month in 1995.
--'Tactical adjustments' are being made to prospective taxation of shipowners, finance and tax ministry officials and teaching staff.

--Some 10,000 clients of insurance firm 'Mesogeios Life' are on hold until a new buyer can be found for the firm's portfolio, estimated at 450-500 million drachmas and staff demand wages outstanding since March.
IMERISIA

--A European Audit Council report on Greece blames mismanagement and wasteful spending in 1991-92 and the subsequent imposition of tens of billions of drachmas in fines for the sorry state of the agricultural sector in Greece.
--Greek workers residing abroad, permanent residents of Greece and expatriate Greeks have deposited more than 20 billion dollars in Greek banks, the central bank revealed yesterday.
--Investigating magistrate Constantinos Ganiatsos, investigating the Delta Securities settlement scandal, confiscated 700,000 shares at the bourse clearing house yesterday.
--The government has approved 840 new investment places, worth a total of 166.5 billion drachmas, with subsidies totalling 69.7 billion.
--The European Investment Bank yesterdy approved a 370 million ECU loan for the Rio-Antirrio project.
KERDOS
--Farmers have rejected the government and industry's call for an end to the blockade and there are now fears that the blockade will continue as long as the prime minister is absent abroad.
--Capital Market Commission President Stelios Thomadakis yesterday said all were to blame for the recent crisis at the Athens Stock Exchange.
--Changes to the uniform public servants' wage scale will mean an average 8.0 percent increase in pay.
EXPRESS
--The British Foreign Office appealed to the government and local government bodies yesterday to find a solution to the blockade which has affected some 100 British lorry drivers.
--Greek telecoms organisation OTE has postponed its decision on a new managing consultant to the end of the week.
--For the first time in at least a year, the Bank of Greece was not forced to intervene in the overnight interbank rate.
--The development ministry is determined to release funds for investment programmes worth 10 billion drachmas tht have not yet been utilised.
NAFTEMBORIKI

--A 5.34 percent fall in overnight stays in the April-October period has rebutted estimates of a major fall in tourism and given rise to hopes for better figures in 1997. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
